n: Ezekiel shaves his head and beard with a sword-sharp blade and weighs the hair into portions. For a priest, shaving was forbidden and shameful—itself a sign of humiliation and mourning.

f.w: upon thine head and upon thy beard

n: One third he burns in the model city, one third he strikes with the blade around it, and one third he scatters to the wind. These stand for those who will die in the siege, those killed by the sword, and those scattered in exile.

f.w: I will draw out a sword after them

n: A few hairs are tucked into his garment’s hem—a small remnant God protects.

f.g: Tie them into the fold of his robe for safekeeping.

n: Even some of the preserved hairs are thrown into the fire. Judgment will continue to touch the survivors too, and fire will spread to all Israel.

f.w: thereof shall a fire come forth into all the house of Israel
f.g: The suffering will touch the whole nation.

n: God interprets: “This is Jerusalem.” He placed her at the center of the nations to be a light and example.

f.w: I have set it in the midst of the nations

n: Instead, Jerusalem rebelled against God’s laws more than the surrounding nations did. Greater light brings greater responsibility.
Israel has not even lived up to the moral standard of its pagan neighbors—a stinging charge.

f.w: neither have done according to the judgments of the nations

n: “I, even I, am against thee.” God himself will carry out judgment in full view of the nations.

f.w: I, even I, am against thee

n: Jerusalem’s judgment will be unlike anything before or after—because of her detestable practices.

f.g: Acts God finds detestable, especially idolatry.

n: Famine will be so extreme that parents and children will eat each other—fulfilling the covenant curses. The survivors will be scattered in every direction.

f.w: the fathers shall eat the sons

n: God swears by his own life: because the temple has been defiled with idols, he will cut Jerusalem down without pity. Chapter 8 shows these abominations in detail.

f.g: A solemn oath formula; God swears by himself.

n: Here the meaning of the hair-sign is spelled out: a third will die of plague and famine, a third by the sword, and a third will be scattered and pursued.
Only after judgment is complete will God’s anger rest. Then the people will recognize that the Lord spoke in his zeal—his passionate, jealous love for his covenant people.

f.g: Or “I will be satisfied”; God’s justice will be fulfilled.
Jealous love, as of a spouse who has been betrayed.

n: Jerusalem will become a ruin and a byword among the nations.
Her fall will be a warning and an object lesson for other nations—an “instruction.”

f.w: a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment

n: Famine is pictured as deadly arrows God shoots, breaking the “staff of bread.”
Famine, wild animals, plague, bloodshed, and sword—the classic covenant curses—will sweep the land.
